sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and knowledge-graph hints: bicycle distances, lane filtering speeds, truck stopping and turning, and the numbers that repeat for farm vehicles and trucks
Look-alike numbers and rules from the road-sharing pages, each tied to one handbook page; hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec15-R01 | anchor: A01
The 3 feet figure is the minimum gap when passing a bicyclist, while the 500 feet figure is how far away a bicycle's white night headlamp must be visible. [A01]
Why it matters: group bicycle numbers; difficulty three; confusable sec15-F05 versus sec15-F15.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-R02 | anchor: A01
Bicyclists normally ride with traffic near the right side, yet they may legally move left to turn left, avoid a hazard, pass, or when the lane is too narrow to share. [A01]
Why it matters: group bicycle position; difficulty two; confusable sec15-F09 versus sec15-F08.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-R03 | anchor: A01
The limit on riding two abreast is about how many bicycles ride side by side, while the passenger limit is about how many people one bicycle may carry. [A01]
Why it matters: group bicycle rules; difficulty two; confusable sec15-F11 versus sec15-F10.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-R04 | anchor: A01
A white headlamp and a rear reflector are required on a bicycle at night, while a flashing red rear light is an optional way to be seen better. [A01]
Why it matters: group bicycle equipment; difficulty two; confusable sec15-F15 versus sec15-F16.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec15-R05 | anchor: A02
For lane filtering, the posted limit may be no higher than 45 miles per hour, while the motorcycle itself may go no faster than 15 miles per hour. [A02]
Why it matters: group lane filtering; difficulty three; confusable sec15-F24 versus sec15-F25.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec15-R06 | anchor: A02
Lane filtering means passing a vehicle stopped in the same lane, and it also needs at least 2 adjacent lanes going the same direction. [A02]
Why it matters: group lane filtering; difficulty two; confusable sec15-F22 versus sec15-F23.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec15-R07 | anchor: A02
A motorcycle tends to look farther away and slower than it really is, which is why drivers turning in front of motorcycles cause most car and motorcycle crashes. [A02]
Why it matters: group motorcycle visibility; difficulty two; confusable sec15-F19 versus sec15-F18.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec15-R08 | anchor: A02
A rider moving to one side may be avoiding a hazard rather than turning, and a blinking motorcycle signal may simply have been left on after a turn. [A02]
Why it matters: group motorcycle intentions; difficulty two; confusable sec15-F27 versus sec15-F29.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec15-R09 | anchor: A03
A truck needs twice as long to stop, and cutting in front of it then braking leaves it only half its stopping distance. [A03]
Why it matters: group truck stopping; difficulty two; confusable sec15-F33 versus sec15-F34.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-R10 | anchor: A03
A truck's wide right turn may leave open space on its right that you must not pass into, while a farm machine may pull left before turning right. [A03]
Why it matters: group wide turns; difficulty three; confusable sec15-F37 versus sec15-F42.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-R11 | anchor: A03
Farm machinery usually travels at 25 mph or less, while a vehicle with the slow-moving vehicle symbol can never exceed 25 mph. [A03]
Why it matters: group slow vehicles; difficulty three; confusable sec15-F41 versus sec15-F43.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]

FACT_ID: sec15-R12 | anchor: A03
The number twenty-five appears both as a truck's weight measured in cars and as a slow-moving vehicle's top speed in mph. [A03]
Why it matters: group numbers; difficulty two; confusable sec15-F39 versus sec15-F43.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0052]
